12.0.s.en: (1) Tobit and his son decide on a reward for Azariah

12.0.0.en: After all these blessings had been received, Tobit the father took his son aside and began to discuss with him the wage that Azariah deserved, the man who had accompanied him on his journey.

12.1.0.en: What should he give him in return for his abundant kindness to Tobias the son?

12.2.0.en: So Tobias the son recalled the five great blessings that Azariah had done for him, which are:

12.2.1.en: 1- He kept him safe and brought him back unharmed from this journey.

12.2.2.en: 2- He recovered the money for him from Gabael.

12.2.3.en: 3- He guided him to Sarah, married him to her, kept Satan away from them, and made her parents rejoice.

12.2.4.en: 4- He rescued him from the fish (that is, the great fish) that was about to devour him.

12.2.5.en: 5- He opened the eyes of Tobit the father.

12.2.6.en: From the foregoing, we see the father and his son appreciating the labor others had undertaken for them, and their gratitude, to the point that they call him holy and resolved to give him half of the possessions they had brought back from the journey.

12.3.0.en: Their humility also appears in their saying: Will Azariah consent and accept half of the possessions?

12.3.1.en: If you are ready to sacrifice and give to God and to others in your time of distress, do not go back on your vows to God or on your promises to others, or on rewarding them for their labor when your problem is solved. Rather, be generous like Tobit and his son, appreciating the labor others have undertaken for you, and give generously, as God also gives to you generously.

12.4.0.en: In humility, Tobit and his son took Azariah aside and begged him to accept half of what they had gained from this journey. We shall see that Azariah will take nothing from them and will make known to them who he is: the glorious archangel Raphael. From this we understand that God's gifts to us are free (Rom 3:24).

12.5.s.en: (2) Azariah asks them to bless God and to declare His work with them

12.5.0.en: The angel, however, spoke to them about something else: that they should glorify God and tell of His works with them.

12.6.0.en: Rather, he made clear to them that, if the secrets of earthly kings ought to be kept hidden, for fear that harm may come to them if they are made known, since they are only men, then, on the contrary, the secrets of the King of kings and Lord of lords, and His work with men, ought to be proclaimed, so that all may bless God, especially in circumstances like those in which the people of God were living, exiled among the Gentiles, so that the children of God might be established in their faith and the Gentiles might see the work of God and believe. But this is on condition that a man does not abandon his humility, boasting when he recalls the works of God, or thinking himself better than others because of what has been done for him. The humility of Tobit and his son was evident, so there was no fear for them in proclaiming the works of God. The secret of the king signifies the mysteries of the Church, which only the faithful see and which are not spoken of or disclosed to unbelievers, for they will not understand them. In addition, the secret of the king is the personal relationship between the soul and God and its private experiences, which are not announced to people, as the Song of Songs says: "A garden inclosed is my sister, my spouse; a spring shut up, a fountain sealed" (Song 4:12). The general rule, then, is that personal experiences are not disclosed, and, when necessary, are attributed to someone unnamed, as the Apostle Paul spoke of a man he knew who was caught up to the third heaven, and he was speaking of himself. But in some cases, for the teaching of others, the teacher needs to declare the secrets of God, and this is done under spiritual guidance, as in the case of Tobit and his son, as the angel instructed them.

12.6.1.en: How beautiful it is for a person to proclaim the works of God while concealing himself, so that he is not fought by pride. So the Apostle Paul in the New Testament declared God's work with him, for God showed him the third heaven, that is, the paradise of bliss, but he hid himself, saying, "I knew a man" and did not say, "I saw" (2 Cor 12:2).

12.7.0.en: After Azariah had called Tobit and his son to bless God and to proclaim His works, he showed them the importance of the three basic means of grace, which are prayer, fasting and almsgiving, and that they are better than all the treasures of the world, because through them a person is joined to God, the source of all spiritual and material wealth.

12.8.0.en: Then he emphasized the importance of almsgiving, since it delivers a person from eternal death, forgives his sins, makes the mercies of God overflow upon him, and through it he inherits eternal life. For almsgiving is a person's going out of himself; then he feels for others and gives to them. This cannot happen except through a person's union with God, his love for Him, his repentance in humility, and his detachment from material things; then he is able to love others and to give himself for them.

12.9.0.en: As for those who are preoccupied with their desires and their selfishness and do many evil things, by this conduct they harm themselves and head toward eternal perdition, through their separation from God, and so they become the worst enemies of themselves.

12.10.s.en: (3) Azariah declares who he is and God's purpose in the life of Tobit

12.10.0.en: Finally, Azariah began to disclose his secret and God's purpose in the life of Tobit, indeed God's purpose in all our lives.

12.11.0.en: He showed how God cares about every act of worship we offer Him, especially fervent prayers that come from the heart, as well as the works of mercy we do, and the preferring of God's works to our own comfort and needs, even essential ones such as food and drink. Tobit did all of these, and the angel offered them up before God immediately, one after another. This shows God's concern for our love toward Him and that He values our works, even if they are small in the eyes of people, such as giving a cup of cold water, how much more if they are great works.

12.12.0.en: And after Tobit's sonship to God and his love for Him had been made evident, God wished to prove him, so that he might have a better place in heaven. So He allowed him the trial of blindness and poverty, and before that, the king's pursuit of him and his attempt to kill him. Yet Tobit stood firm in his faith and in his love for God.

12.12.1.en: Likewise Sarah also stood firm in her faith in God, despite the failure of her seven marriages.

12.13.0.en: And finally the angel declared that God had sent him to heal Tobit the father of his blindness, and Sarah, his son's wife (his daughter-in-law), of Satan's assault on any man who tried to marry her.

12.13.1.en: Thus it is shown that God, the Almighty, watches all our works with care and allows trial only for our good, and only for a time. Then He removes it from us and blesses us with more abundant blessings.

12.14.0.en: And finally Azariah revealed his true identity, which is that he is the archangel Raphael, one of the seven archangels who stand before God.

12.15.s.en: (4) The fear of Tobit and his son, and the angel's reassurance of them

12.15.0.en: At this heavenly declaration they fell on their faces to the ground, trembling with great fear, when they realized that they were in the presence of the great archangel Raphael. This shows their humility and the fear of God that was in their hearts.

12.16.0.en: So the angel reassured them and gave them peace, and explained to them that his appearing, his accompanying Tobias the son, and everything he had done with them were by God's providence and will.

12.17.0.en: Then he explained to them that his human conduct in eating and drinking and all the material things he had done was merely an outward appearance, but in truth he has no need of these foods or of anything material, since his spiritual food is the love of God and prayer. And let us know that the stronger and higher being (the spiritual) can easily resemble the lesser creature (the material) in eating, drinking, walking, sleeping, and so on; on the contrary, a material creature, such as a human being or an animal, cannot resemble spiritual creatures, that is, the angels. Yet a human being, since he is a spiritual and material creature, can share with the angels in some works, such as prayer, love and self-giving.

12.18.0.en: Then the glorious archangel Raphael bade them farewell and stressed two things: blessing and glorifying the Lord, and then speaking of God's works to others, so that they may believe and be established in their faith.

12.19.0.en: After the angel ascended to heaven and disappeared from sight, Tobit and his son remained prostrate before God, in reverence, offering prayers of thanksgiving and blessing God for three hours, with feelings of fear and joy mingled together within them. Then they rose in joy and began to tell all their relatives and loved ones of the greatness of God with them.

12.19.1.en: Thus we see that beholding heavenly things is something very great, which required the father and his son to remain prostrate before God for three hours, and the number three points to the fullness of reverence. How much more, then, should our feeling be when we approach the Holy Sacraments, such as the sacrament of confession and the sacrament of Holy Communion? In the story of Tobit we find the clearest appearance of the glorious archangel Raphael in the Holy Bible, and the Fathers interpret other appearances in the Holy Bible as being of the angel Raphael, and they are:-

12.19.2.en: 1- The appearance of an angel to Christ to strengthen Him in the Garden of Gethsemane (Lk 22:39-43), for the angel Raphael is the angel of help. Thus the angel Raphael served Christ, to whom Tobit points as a type, just as he served Tobit, who is a symbol of Christ.

12.19.3.en: 2- The appearance of an angel who stirred the water in the pool of Bethesda (Jn 5:1-4). The angel Raphael is also called the angel of healing.

12.19.4.en: The closing prayer of Tobit the father

13.0.0.en: After glorifying God, who is glorified forever, he declared that it is part of God's mercy that He allows affliction and then returns and has mercy on us.

13.1.0.en: And if He allows a wound, He returns and heals it, and if a person feels that he has gone down to the depths, God returns and lifts him up, has mercy on him and honors him. This gives hope to everyone in affliction: let him be assured that it will pass and that God's tender hand will have mercy on him, and a person feels the fatherhood of God, who does not allow our affliction to the end, but only for a time. Therefore, when King David sinned by numbering the people and becoming proud, and deserved punishment, and God asked him to choose a punishment, he said, let me fall into the hand of God and not into the hand of men, trusting in the mercy of God, who returns and removes his affliction from him (2 Sam 24:14). By this verse God removes from minds the pagan idea that proclaims a god of good and a god of evil; He is the one God, the Almighty, who gives good things and allows evils, for everything is in His hand alone, and He has affirmed this meaning in other places of the Holy Bible, such as (Isa 40:7; 1 Sam 2:6-8).

13.2.0.en: Then one of God's purposes in the affliction of His people is shown, in allowing them to go into captivity: that they might proclaim God among the Gentiles, by their pure lives and good conduct, their confession of God and their speaking of His works, so that the Gentiles might believe in God.

13.2.1.en: And this is a clear declaration that God offers His salvation to the whole world and not only to the Jews.

13.3.0.en: He also declares that the cause of the affliction is the sins of the people, but God, in His love, has mercy on them and removes the affliction from them when they repent.

13.4.0.en: Then he calls to his people, after they have seen God's work with him, to glorify God and confess His holiness in continual prayers and constant thanksgiving, and by this their conduct becomes upright and glorifies God. This means that whoever prays much from his heart has his life purified and walks uprightly according to the will of God.

13.5.0.en: Then Tobit continues his prayer by praising God and glorifying Him, because He has mercy on His people who sinned against Him, and this shows the extent of His mercy. The importance of this praise is that it takes place in captivity, that is, Tobit praises God while still in affliction, a captive who has not yet returned to his homeland. How beautiful it is to praise God at all times, even in times of distress.

13.5.1.en: God also shows the Gentiles the greatness of His people and His hatred of sin, such that He disciplines His beloved people who believe in Him; by this He calls the Gentiles to believe in Him and to turn away from the sin that angers Him, and if they do not repent, He will discipline them and take vengeance on them.

13.6.0.en: Then Tobit calls all sinners to return to God with a pure life, confident of His mercy toward them, for He "will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth" (1 Tim 2:4).

13.7.0.en: Then he calls all the children of God to join with his own rejoicing soul in praising and glorifying God, and even to set aside whole days for praise and joy.

13.7.1.en: Praise God first, and your heart will be filled with joy, and then you will be able to call others to praise.

13.8.s.en: (2) His prophecy of the return of greatness to Jerusalem

13.8.0.en: Here in his prayer Tobit addresses Jerusalem, the great city in which is the temple of God. It also signifies the human soul and signifies the Church. So he says to Jerusalem, or to his own soul, that because of the multitude of sin God condemned it and allowed it affliction and captivity.

13.9.0.en: But with steadfast hope he says to her, give thanks to God and bless Him. And how can a person bless God while in affliction, unless he is confident of God's mercy, and his hope in Him is steadfast, certain that He will remove this affliction from him? Therefore he says to Jerusalem that the ruined temple in her will be built again, her captive children will return to her, and she will rejoice forever.

13.9.1.en: This is what happens with the repentant human soul, which feels that the affliction is because of its sins, thanks God for everything, and trusts that God will return and build His dwelling within it, reign over it, fill its heart, and bring back to it all its captive children, that is, its senses, thoughts and all its members, returning pure, as members of Christ, and it lives a life of joy and constant praise.

13.10.0.en: "You will shine with a glad radiance": you will glow with a joyful light.

13.10.2.en: Then he promises Jerusalem that she will be exalted above all the nations and will shine with greatness, joy and splendor that dazzle the eyes, so that all peoples will bow before her in reverence, worshiping in esteem and respect; indeed, the nations will bring her gifts and will feel that she is a holy land in which God dwells.

13.10.3.en: And history bears witness to this, for Alexander the Great, when he reached Jerusalem, felt the greatness of the temple, bowed down before it and offered his sacrifices.

13.10.4.en: And these words are a prophecy of the Gentiles' faith in Christianity and their worship in the new Jerusalem, that is, the Church, which believers from all the peoples of the world enter.

13.10.5.en: And this is what happens with the soul over which God reigns: He glorifies it among men on earth, and also in heaven, and gives it awe in the eyes of all, so that they seek its good pleasure, since they feel that God dwells in it.

13.11.0.en: And for the glorifying of the great name of God in you, O Jerusalem, whoever despises and scorns you, the curse of God comes upon him, but he who honors you and builds you up, God blesses.

13.11.1.en: Thus, when God dwells in a person and is glorified in his works, all the wicked who persecute him are cursed by God, that is, the punishment of God comes upon them, even if after a while, and then their punishment is completed in eternal torment. But he who honors the spiritual person and works for his edification, God blesses.

13.12.0.en: Then he continues his prayer, calling Jerusalem to rejoice in her children gathered in her around the Lord, and the Lord blesses her.

13.13.0.en: Then he pronounces blessed those who love Jerusalem and seek her good and peace.

13.14.0.en: And he calls himself among the lovers of Jerusalem, to bless the Lord for His mercy and for the deliverance of Jerusalem from destruction.

13.14.1.en: So also the human soul rejoices in the gathering of all its members and senses around the Lord, and exults in worshiping Him, praising Him and working for His good pleasure. Likewise the Lord blesses those who fear Him and all who love them, and all the lovers of the Lord thank Him for His love and mercy toward His children. The Church also rejoices in the gathering of her children in her, praising God. And everyone who loves the Church and seeks her peace, the Lord blesses, and all the lovers of the Church glorify God for His works and His mercy to His Church.

13.15.0.en: And finally, he closes his prayer with prophecies about the coming glory of Jerusalem, and pronounces himself blessed if any of his descendants remain to see this glory. Here he prophesies about the glory of Jerusalem in her return from captivity, and also about the Incarnation of Christ and His redemption of His Church, and in the end he prophesies about the heavenly Jerusalem, so we find a clear similarity between his prophecies and the words of the Revelation of John the Theologian in the New Testament.

13.16.0.en: He prophesies about the gates of Jerusalem, that is, her entrances. They are of sapphire, whose color is blue, the color of heaven, meaning that those who enter her will have the thought and the pure spiritual life of heaven. It is also a hard stone, which signifies spiritual firmness, strength and patience, and it is purified by fire, because the children of the Kingdom bear the cross and endure many sufferings, and so are crowned in heaven.

13.16.1.en: The gates are also of emerald. Its color is green, and it signifies freshness and vitality, meaning that those who enter her through their spiritual striving and the work of the Holy Spirit in them grow in the knowledge of God and live with Him forever. After that he speaks about the walls of the city. The walls are what surround the city, fortify it and keep every harm from it, and they are made of precious stones, that is, of the most precious thing, for nothing is more precious than the name of the Lord and the blood of Christ the Redeemer, who saves us from death and by whom we take refuge from all the wars of the devil, as the Holy Bible says, "The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe" (Prov 18:10).

13.17.0.en: He continues his prophecies about Jerusalem, or about the human soul that lives with God, or about the Church, and describes her streets as paved with pure white stone. The streets are the place where people gather, so he declares that the gathering of her children is marked by purity, and their dealings by uprightness and splendor (white). And the stone points to strength and firmness, meaning that her children enjoy spiritual firmness and a strong life with God, so they are not shaken by the changes of life, but live in steadfast faith.

13.17.1.en: And in the streets of the city (that is, the roads that connect her various parts) they sing Hallelujah, which signifies that the praise of the name of the Lord is what binds the children of this city to one another.

13.18.0.en: And at the end he blesses God, who glorified Jerusalem, or His Church, or the souls that love Him, and even exalted her above the whole world, by His reigning over her forever, so that He gives her joy in His fellowship and His love. The end of Tobit's life and his final testament
